data.one_liner: Make HTTP requests using Rust and reqwest via FFI for Flutter apps
data.what_it_does: Allows Flutter apps to make HTTP requests using a Rust backend through FFI. It provides support for HTTP/1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3, TLS 1.2/1.3, connection pooling, interceptors, and compatibility with standard dart:io, http, and dio APIs.
use_when: You need high-performance HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 support across Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, and Linux
You want a unified API for HTTP requests that also supports Windows and Linux
You need advanced networking features like certificate pinning, custom DNS resolution, and connection pooling
avoid_when: You are building for the web platform, which is currently not supported
You want to avoid the build complexity and size overhead of adding a Rust toolchain and FFI bindings to your Flutter project
strengths: Supports HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 with reliable performance powered by Rust's reqwest crate
Cross-platform support including desktop operating systems like Windows and Linux
Compatible with existing http and dio client patterns
weaknesses: Requires Rust toolchain installed and increases APK/app size
data.setup_notes: Requires installing Rust via rustup (1.80.0 or later), Android NDK / Command-line tools, and calling Rhttp.init() during app start.

alternatives.name: http
alternatives.why_pick_it: You want a pure Dart, lightweight HTTP package without Rust dependencies or complex native setup.

alternatives.name: dio
alternatives.why_pick_it: You prefer a feature-rich, pure Dart HTTP client with interceptors, global configuration, and FormData support.
